claims.behaviour: Column types are offered under these groups, listed by ascending order value (key, title, order): `featured` Featured 0; `progress` Progress 200; `structure` Structure 250; `fields` Fields 300; `icons` Icons 350; `totals` Totals 400; `formulas` Calculated 450; `advanced` Advanced 500; `pages` Page Fields 500; `tempo` Tempo 550; the empty key Other Columns 10000. The group titles are i18n texts resolved when shown.

The column types known to the grid and their spec keys are: `main`, `attribute`, `rowid`, `itemid`, `semantics`, `actions`, `field` (also accepts `timeAggregate`), `handle`, `icons` (also accepts `joined`), `progress`, `worklogged`, `seq`, `formula`, `notes`, `blank`, `timeinstatus`, `query-match`, `comment`, `tempo-worklogged`, `tempo-timeplanned`, and `pages` (Confluence page fields). They are registered through the public column type registry, so a companion app's column types sit beside them. The two Tempo types are created with the widget's start-up context. Registration of the built-in set happens once per page: starting a second widget on the same page does not register anything twice; `pages` and its group are registered when the script loads, before the others.

Column key `blank` is a separator. Its cells and header are empty. Its width is fixed at 6 px (current, minimum and default), it cannot be resized, and a width stored for it is ignored. Its cells never flash. It has no entry in the add-column menu and no configurator, so it only appears when a view's specification contains it.

Column key `rowid`: each cell shows the row's numeric id as text (negative for an unsaved row). Default name and type name: Row ID. It is offered in the add-column menu as `{key: rowid}` in the Structure group, and can be picked as a column type. No parameters, no options, no attributes requested, not sortable. Auto-size is allowed and it can shrink when there is no space.

Column key `itemid`: each cell shows the row's item id, HTML-escaped, with the leading `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-` removed when present. Examples: `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-folder/12` shows `folder/12`; `10003` (an issue) shows `10003`; `com.almworks.structure.pages:type-confluence-page/5` shows in full. Default name and type name: Item ID. Offered in the add-column menu as `{key: itemid}` in the Structure group. No parameters, no options, no attributes requested, not sortable. Auto-size is allowed and it can shrink when there is no space.

Column key `semantics` shows how the row got into the forest: `title`, `group`, `ins` or `ext` for the row semantics values 1, 2, 3 and 4 (title, group, inserted, extension); any other non-zero value shows as itself, HTML-escaped; no semantics shows nothing. Default name and type name: Semantics. It is offered in the add-column menu and as a type to switch to only when the page runs in debug mode (URL fragment parameter `debug`); otherwise an existing column of this key still renders. The configurator places it in the Fields group. No options, no attributes requested, not sortable. Auto-size is allowed and it can shrink when there is no space.

Column key `seq` requests attribute `seq` in format `text` on the `unfiltered` forest, whatever the panel's current filters, and shows the value HTML-escaped (for example `1.2.3`), empty when there is none. So numbering does not change when a filter hides rows. Filtering therefore leaves gaps in the numbers rather than renumbering.

Column key `seq`: the header's default name is Index, the type name and the add-column entry read Sequential Index, in the Structure group. The preset and the type switch give `{key: seq}`. No parameters, no options. Not sortable; auto-size is allowed; it does not shrink when there is no space; default width 120, minimum 27. The attribute picker offers `seq` in format `text` as a suggestion taken from this column.

Column key `comment` shows the latest comment: it requests attribute `comment` in format `html` and shows the value unescaped, empty when there is none. Sorting uses attribute `comment` in format `order`, through the generic attribute sorter. It suggests `comment` in format `text` to the attribute picker. Auto-size is allowed and it can shrink when there is no space.

The `comment` column's name, type name and add-column entry are Last Comment, in the Fields group. Its preset and type switch give `{key: comment, params: {}}`. The configurator shows no input, only the line 'The column shows the last comment for the issue.' A column spec with any other key gives neither a column nor a configurator.

Column key `attribute` is saved as `{key: attribute, params: {attribute: {id, format, params?}, format?, forestSpec?}}`. The display format is `params.format`, else `params.attribute.format`, else `html`. An attribute with no id, or whose registered descriptor rejects its parameters, counts as absent. An attribute id with no registered descriptor counts as valid.
A column with no valid attribute shows empty cells, requests no attribute, cannot be sorted, does not flash and suggests nothing to the attribute picker.
A column with a valid attribute requests it with the display format in place of its own format, on the forest named by `params.forestSpec` (displayed when unset).

The cell reads the value of the attribute as saved (its own format, on `params.forestSpec`). With display format `html` the value is shown unescaped, with any other format it is converted to text and HTML-escaped. A falsy value shows an empty cell, including the number 0 and the boolean false.

When `params.format` differs from `params.attribute.format`, the column requests the attribute in `params.format` but reads and flashes it under `params.attribute.format`, so the cell stays empty (as the original does).

Sorting an `attribute` column: with display format `number` it sorts by the attribute as saved; otherwise, if the attribute's descriptor supports format `order`, it sorts by a copy of the attribute with format `order`; otherwise the column is not sortable. The first sort is descending when the descriptor supports format `number`, otherwise ascending.

The `attribute` column's default name is the attribute registry's suggested label for the attribute (a preset's name when the spec matches a preset, else the descriptor's label); with none it is Attribute. The type name is Attribute.

The `attribute` type adds these add-column entries, in this order (label, group, spec params): 'Attribute...' in Advanced with `{attribute: {}}`, which opens the configurator at once; 'Count Sub-Items' in Structure with `{attribute: {id: count, format: html}}`; 'Count Leaves' in Structure with `{attribute: {id: count, format: html, params: {leaves: true}}}`; 'Status Category' in Advanced with `{attribute: {id: status-category, format: html}}`; 'Project Category' in Advanced with `{attribute: {id: project-category, format: html}}`; 'Transition Date (In Progress)' in Progress with `{attribute: {id: transition-date, format: html, params: {category: indeterminate, transition: first}}}`; 'Transition Date (Done)' in Progress with `{attribute: {id: transition-date, format: html, params: {category: done, transition: latest}}}`. Switching type gives `{key: attribute, params: {attribute: {}}}`.

The `attribute` configurator has one option, titled Attribute, which edits `params.attribute` with the attribute picker. Its panel is the wide one, and it is resizable only while the chosen attribute's id is `expr`. Opening the column or its presets first waits for the attribute registry's metadata.

An `attribute` column allows auto-size, can shrink when there is no space, flashes when its attribute changes, and suggests a copy of its attribute to the attribute picker. Default width 120, minimum 27.

Column key `icons` is saved as `{key: icons, params: {fields: [...]}}`. It exists only when `params.fields` is an array, every entry is a Jira field the user can see, and every entry is one of `project`, `issuetype`, `priority`, `reporter`, `assignee`. Otherwise no column is created.

For each entry of `fields` the column requests attribute `<field>.icon` in format `html`. The cell shows those values unescaped, side by side in the order of `fields`, leaving out empty ones. No `fields` gives an empty cell.

An `icons` column's default width is 16 px per field plus 32 px, counting 6 fields when there are none: 64 for 2 fields, 112 for 5, 128 for none. Auto-size is not allowed. It can shrink when there is no space. Not sortable. Minimum width 27.

The add-column menu has two `icons` entries, both in the Icons group: 'TP' with `fields` `[issuetype, priority]` and column name TP; 'All Icons' with `fields` `[project, issuetype, priority, reporter, assignee]` and no column name, so its header reads Icons. An entry is left out when any of its fields is not available in Jira. Switching type gives `{key: icons, params: {}}`. Default and type name: Icons.

The `icons` configurator has one option, Fields: a vertical list of checkboxes labelled with the Jira field name. The saved fields come first in their order, then the remaining fields of the five, and fields unknown to Jira are left out. Each row has a drag handle with the tooltip 'Drag to change icon order'. Rows drag only up and down.

Ticking or unticking a field, or dropping a row, rewrites `params.fields` as the ticked fields in their current list order. The configuration is valid only with at least one field ticked. Reopening shows the saved order.

A saved column of key `joined` whose `fields` array holds only `issuetype` and `priority` (or is empty) is treated as an `icons` column with the same fields, on a copy of the spec; a saved name goes through i18n template rendering first, so `{...}` keys in it are resolved. The view keeps the key `joined` until the column is changed in its configurator, which saves key `icons`.

Any other column of key `joined` exists when `params.fields` is an array of Jira fields the user can see (any fields). For each entry it requests attribute `<field>` in format `html`, and the cell shows the values unescaped, joined with nothing between them, leaving out empty ones. Auto-size is allowed, it can shrink when there is no space, and it is not sortable.

A `joined` column has no default name, so its header is empty unless the spec names it. Its type name is Multiple Fields, it is in the Icons group, and its configurator has no options. It has no add-column entry: it only comes from saved views.

The `handle` column's width is fixed: 70 px, 56 px on the Jira Software tab, 32 px in a remote gadget, plus 16 px while duplicate icons are shown. The same number is its current, minimum and default width. It cannot be resized, a stored width is ignored, and it never shows the placeholder for an absent value.

The `handle` column requests `done` and `editable` in format `boolean` and `children-automations-hint` in format `html`, and also `manually-adjusted` in format `boolean` while the panel's layout option for the adjustment icon is on.

Outside a remote gadget each handle cell has a drag handle, a selection mark and the status marks. The selection mark is a link whose accessible label is 'Selection mark of row <rowId>'; clicking it toggles that row's selection and focuses the panel (a Shift-only click does nothing). In a remote gadget the cell has only the status marks, without drag handle or selection mark.
The `handle` column's header holds a toggle that selects or clears all rows; in a remote gadget the header is empty.

The status mark of a row is chosen in this order, and the first match ends it: (1) upload error mark; (2) on the Jira Software tab nothing further; (3) in history mode the history mark (see `handle-history-mark`), or an empty placeholder for an unchanged row; (4) on a planning task the planning mark, tooltip 'This item is only available in Structure.'; (5) otherwise the done mark, followed by at most one of the marks in `handle-extra-marks`.

A warning mark is shown when the row has failed uploads in the upload queue, or when the row is edited and its upload failed. Its tooltip is 'Creation of this issue failed. Click to open editor.' for a new row (negative id) and 'We failed to upload the changes to this item. Click to open editor.' otherwise. Clicking the mark of a row with failed uploads in the queue opens the widget's question popup for the problem.

In history mode a changed row shows a mark for its change. The change kind comes from the history manager (claimed with it), and the tooltip by kind is: added 'This item was added', movedTo 'This item was moved here', movedFrom 'This item was moved from here', removed 'This item was removed', copied 'This item was copied'.

The check mark is present in every row that reaches step 5 of the mark order, with the tooltip 'The work on the item is completed', and is visible only in rows whose `done` attribute is true. A row with `done` true also gets the done row state, which other parts of the grid style.

After the done mark at most one more is added, first match wins: a pencil, tooltip 'This item has been edited, but the changes have not yet been uploaded.', when the row has local edits or external dirty data; a lock, tooltip 'You cannot add, remove or rearrange immediate sub-items of this issue', when `editable` is exactly false, the item is an issue and the panel respects parent edit permission; on the <product> Board, when `children-automations-hint` has a value, an automation mark whose tooltip is the hint rendered as an automation summary.

While the panel shows duplicate icons, every handle cell starts with a duplicate slot. With the item appearing once or less in the panel's statistics the slot is an empty placeholder. Appearing more than once, it shows the tooltip 'This item is shown <n> times' and a mark in one of these states: with transforms enabled and nothing pinned, hover-only and clickable; with transforms enabled and this item pinned, filled and clickable; with another item pinned, outlined and not clickable; with transforms disabled, outlined and not clickable.
Clicking a clickable duplicate mark focuses that row and toggles the pin of its item, and the click goes no further.
While the adjustment icon option is on, the drag handle of a row whose `manually-adjusted` is true shows as adjusted.

Cells of summable columns (field columns with a sum, query-match, formula, worklogged and the like) show the row's total, and also its own value when they differ. Both values are compared as trimmed text. With an own value and no total, the own value is shown as the main one. With an equal own value and total, only the total shows. With different ones, the total comes first and the own value second in a secondary style, and the cell has the tooltip 'This issue's own value is shown in gray'.

A summable column has a sum exactly when `params.aggregate` is `sum`. The sum attribute is `{id: sum, format: <number unless given>, params: {attribute: <the summed attribute>}}`, with `distinct: true` in `params` when `params.distinct` is true.
With `params.aggregate` = `sum` a summable column's default name is the sum sign, a space and the base name: `Σ Query match`.

The aggregate option has the checkbox 'Sum over sub-items', and below it, only while that is ticked, 'Exclude duplicates' and 'After filtering'. Ticked it stores `params.aggregate` = `sum`, `params.forestSpec` = `displayed` when 'After filtering' is ticked and `unfiltered` when not, and `params.distinct` as true or false. Unticked it removes all three. 'After filtering' shows ticked when `forestSpec` is empty or `displayed`, unticked otherwise. Ticking the sum on a column that had none leaves both lower boxes unticked, which stores `unfiltered` and `distinct` false.

On a field column the aggregate option is shown only for summable fields. When the chosen field stops being summable, the three boxes are cleared, the option is hidden and `aggregate`, `forestSpec` and `distinct` are removed from the params.

Column key `field` is saved as `{key: field, params: {field, aggregate?, distinct?, forestSpec?, compact?, view?}}`. A column exists only when `params.field` is a Jira field known to the user and `aggregate` is absent, or is `sum` on a summable field. Anything else, including an `aggregate` of another value, gives no column.

A saved column of key `timeAggregate` is read as `field` with `aggregate` = `sum`, on a copy of the spec. The view keeps the old key until the column is changed in its configurator, which saves key `field`.

A field is summable when it is `worklogged`, or a system field of type number or duration (`votes`, `watches`, `timespent`, `timeoriginalestimate`, `timeestimate`), or a numeric custom field other than the types `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:importid`, `com.pyxis.greenhopper.jira:gh-global-rank` and `com.pyxis.greenhopper.jira:greenhopper-ranking`.

A field column other than `issuekey` requests one attribute in format `html`: for `customfield_<n>` with n a non-zero integer, `{id: customfield, params: {fieldId: n}}`; for anything else, `{id: <field id>}`. On a Jira field of type user, its `params` also carry `view` from the column. If the Jira configuration lists a field `key`, a column of it uses attribute `key` in format `html` and takes its field properties from `issuekey`.

With a sum, a field column also requests `{id: sum, format: html, params: {attribute: <the same attribute without view, in format duration for timespent, timeoriginalestimate, timeestimate, and number otherwise>}}`, with `distinct: true` when `params.distinct` is set. All of the column's attributes are requested on the forest in `params.forestSpec`.

Sort of a field column, first match wins: `issuekey` by `{id: key, format: order}`; a column with a sum by its sum attribute in the summed format (`duration` or `number`), not `html`; a sortable system field by `{id: <field>, format: order}`; a custom field by its attribute in format `order`; anything else cannot be sorted. Not sortable system fields: `thumbnail`, `issuelinks`, `subtasks`. Fields outside the known system list, such as a companion app's, are not sortable either.

Sorting by a custom field first waits for the Jira configuration to load. If the field is one of the Jira Software rank fields, the column sorts with transform module `com.almworks.jira.structure:sorter-agile-rank`, params `{fieldId: <n>}`. Any other custom field uses `com.almworks.jira.structure:sorter-attribute`, params `{attribute: <the sort attribute>}`, which is also what every other sortable field uses. Without Jira Software there are no rank fields.

The first sort is descending for `versions`, `fixVersions`, `priority`, `created`, `updated`, `duedate`, `resolutiondate`, `votes`, `watches`, `timespent`, `timeoriginalestimate`, `timeestimate` and for every `customfield_...` field, and ascending for all others.

A field column of `issuekey` requests `key` and `url` in format `text`, and with `params.compact` true also `project.icon` in format `html`. An empty key gives an empty cell. Otherwise the content is the HTML-escaped key, or in compact view with a project icon: for a key with exactly one dash, the icon then the part after the dash (`ABC-123` shows the icon and `123`); for another key containing a colon, the icon then the whole key; for another key, only the icon. In compact view with no icon the plain key shows.

When `url` has a value, the key cell's content is a link to it. For an issue row it is a Jira issue link carrying the issue key, so Jira's issue hover and link handlers work on it; for other rows it is a plain link. With no `url` there is no link.

Field cells other than `issuekey` show the attribute value unescaped. All field cells follow the total-and-own rules of `summable-cell`. In a cell with a failed edit an error triangle appears at the end, with the error text as tooltip, while the editor has edited data or is active. While the editor loads, a loading indicator comes before the content. Every field cell except `thumbnail` also carries the overflow control.

For field `thumbnail`, a value containing images is post-processed: an image with both width and height attributes and height above 26 gets height 26 and its width scaled in proportion, rounded. Its enclosing link gets target `imageAttachment` and rel `thumbnail_<rowId>`, but these changes reach the page only if at least one image in the value was scaled; otherwise the value is shown unchanged. A click on the image opens the panel's image gallery, and the focused row's thumbnail can also be opened by a keyboard action.
A field column's default name is the Jira field's name, or `Σ <name>` with a sum on a summable field. For a field unknown to Jira it is empty. The type name is Field.
With a sum, a field cell flashes only when the sum attribute changes on the column's forest. Without one, it flashes when any of its attributes changes.
A field column allows auto-size, can shrink when there is no space, default width 120, minimum 27.
A field column suggests to the attribute picker a copy of its sum attribute when it has one, else its attribute; for `issuekey` nothing.

With the Assets app present, after rendering a cell of an Assets object field (the object, default object, object multi, object reference, object reference multi and read-only object custom field types of `com.riadalabs.jira.plugins.insight`), outside gadgets, the UI looks for Assets object elements in the cell. If any is not yet initialized, it calls the Assets client function `RLABS.CustomField.initializeCustomField(undefined, <cell element>)`. Without the app, or when that function is missing, nothing happens and the value shows as sent by the server.

In a gadget, for user fields, `issuetype` and `priority`: while the cell's editor is active the UI sets Jira's page parameter `ignoreFrame` to true, so Jira's pickers can leave the gadget frame; once the cell is no longer edited, it removes that parameter.

A field column's cell can be edited as follows. For an issue row: never for the read-only Assets object custom field; in a gadget, only for `issuetype`, `security`, `assignee`, `priority`, `timeoriginalestimate`, `timeestimate`, numeric custom fields, and custom fields of the types `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:textarea`, `com.deniz.jira.customfields:single-select` and `com.deniz.jira.customfields:multi-select`; elsewhere for every field except `issuekey`, `project`, `resolution`, `created`, `updated`, `resolutiondate`, `votes`, `watches`, `timespent`, `workratio`, `thumbnail`, `issuelinks`, `subtasks`. For a memo or planning task row: any field the column shows. For other item types: none.

For deciding whether an issue cell can be edited, the UI consults the cached field renderers of the issue, under the field's editing name. The field counts as known to be not editable when the renderers have no entry for it, the entry has no edit HTML (no create HTML for a new row), or the field is `timeoriginalestimate` and the renderers say the original estimate cannot be changed. On a new row, `issuetype` is always not editable through this column. While the renderers are not cached, or a new row has no normalized creation context, the field is not considered known to be uneditable.

The add-column menu has one entry per Jira field given by the configuration: `{key: field, params: {field: <id>}}`, followed for a summable field by `{key: field, params: {field: <id>, aggregate: sum}}`. Switching type gives `{key: field, params: {}}`.

A field column belongs in group Tempo when its field is a Tempo account or team custom field (`com.tempoplugin.tempo-accounts:accounts.customfield`, `com.tempoplugin.tempo-teams:team.customfield`); otherwise in Totals with an aggregate; otherwise in Fields.

The field configurator's options, in order: Field, then the aggregate option, then Compact View, then the user view. Field is a single-select of all Jira fields by name. With no field saved, the list starts with an empty entry, which disappears on the first choice. The configuration is invalid until a field is chosen. Changing the field keeps the other params.
The checkbox 'Compact View' is shown only for field `issuekey`. It stores `params.compact` as true or false.

For Jira fields of type user, the configurator has radio buttons 'Photo only', 'Name only', 'Photo + Name', stored in `params.view` as `avatar`, `name`, `both`. Unset shows as 'Photo + Name', and the option is hidden for other fields. The value goes to the server in the attribute's `view` parameter, so changing it re-requests the column.

Column key `main` is saved as `{key: main, params: {description?, icons?, showNonIssueAttributes?, showProjectLead?}}`. Each param is stored only when it differs from its default, and `params` is removed when it becomes empty.

The `main` configurator has four checkboxes, in order: 'Show Description' (`description`, default ticked), 'Show Icons' (`icons`, default ticked), 'Show Sprint and Version attributes' (`showNonIssueAttributes`, default unticked), 'Show Project Lead' (`showProjectLead`, default unticked). The type name is Item, and the default column name is the Jira `summary` field's name (empty in the configurator when it is unavailable; Item in the grid).

The `main` column's default width is 250 px; its minimum is 200 px, or 100 px on the Jira Software tab. It can shrink when there is no space, and auto-size is not used. Clicking its header does not sort by a column value (see the table header's claims).

The `main` column always requests `summary` and `url` in format `text`, `key` in format `text`, `extended-summary` in format `html`, and the aggregated versions `{id: summary, format: text, params: {aggregate: true}}` and `{id: icon, format: html, params: {aggregate: true}}`. It also requests: `icon` in format `html` unless `icons` is false; `basic-generation-info` in format `json` when `lozenge` is set; `description` in format `html` and its aggregated version unless `description` is false; `version-start`, `version-release`, `sprint-start`, `sprint-end` in format `text` and `version-description`, `sprint-goal` in format `html` when `showNonIssueAttributes` is true; `project-lead` in format `html` when `showProjectLead` is true.
A column `main` reads the widget's 'automation shown' switch when created and follows it. Each change tells the panel its columns changed, which re-requests attributes and repaints.

A row counts as having data to show when it has a non-empty `summary` (text) or `extended-summary` (html). A row without such data, while it may show an absent value, gets only an indent in the main cell: the depth offset plus 33 px, with no text.

A main cell shows in order: the overflow control; an indent according to depth; the expander; the icon; the summary; the extra attributes; the load error; the generation label; the edit error. The expander is left out on a title row (semantics 1) and while the cell shows an inline edit error.

When the row's cell editor has errors and no open input, and either the error was not flashed yet or the editor panel is visible, the main cell uses the error layout: indent of 6 px instead of the depth indent, no expander, no extra attributes.
With an error text while the editor has edited data or is active, the main cell shows an error triangle with that text as tooltip, placed at the depth offset plus 22 px, or at 0 in the error layout.
For an item the user cannot access, the summary, extra attributes and generation label are hidden and the text 'Unavailable item' shows in their place. The icon and expander stay.

With `icons` not false, every main cell has an icon slot. It shows the `icon` value; with none, the default icon of the item type: issue a horizontal ellipsis; folder and text a folder; structure the structure icon; component, group, Confluence page, sprint and Tempo account each their own icon; any other type a 'no icon' placeholder. A label row always shows a tag, a loop marker row always a loop icon. A version-name row shows only the aggregated `icon` value, or the placeholder.
The default summary is the trimmed `summary` text, HTML-escaped: as a link to `url` when `url` has a value (an item link), otherwise plain text; with an empty summary, an ellipsis character.
For an issue with `summary`, `url` and `key` all present, the summary is an untrimmed Jira issue link to `url` carrying the key. If one is missing, the default rules apply.

For generators and effectors, the summary is `extended-summary` rendered as an automation summary; with no `extended-summary` the default summary shows. Rendering automation summaries may repaint the cell once the attribute registry's metadata arrives.

Other item types: a label shows `summary` as a single label lozenge, or nothing without one; a status shows `extended-summary` as HTML with no link; a memo and a planning task show `summary` as plain text on the issue page, in a gadget and on the Jira Software tab, and elsewhere as a link to `#`; a version name uses the aggregated `summary`.

Extra attributes are shown only if at least one of Show Description, Show Sprint and Version attributes and Show Project Lead is on, and not in the error layout or for inaccessible items. By type: issue, memo and planning task show `description`; version name the aggregated `description`; version `version-start`, `version-release`, `version-description` with 'Show Sprint and Version attributes'; sprint `sprint-start`, `sprint-end`, `sprint-goal` with the same option; project `project-lead` with 'Show Project Lead'. Other types show none.

Each extra attribute shows after the summary, trimmed; empty ones are left out. The value is preceded by a label and a space: `sprint-start` 'Start date', `sprint-end` 'End date', `version-start` 'Start date', `version-release` 'Release date', `project-lead` 'Lead'; others have none. Values of format `html` are shown unescaped, others escaped. Each carries its attribute id and format so that other UI can find it.

With the column param `lozenge` set, and for accessible items, the cell shows a subtle lozenge with the `label` of `basic-generation-info`. It shows as 'complete' when `creator` is `extender`, as 'moved' when `grouper`, plain otherwise. No value or no label shows nothing. No configurator option sets this param.

Editing the main cell uses a single-line text input named `summary`, 255 characters at most, browser autocomplete off, prefilled with the `summary` text. It is at least 300 px wide, and otherwise as wide as the cell allows. If the summary text has not arrived yet, the editor does not open. A new row needs no server data and its input is not resized. An existing row first loads the item's editing data for `summary` when that is not available yet, and a load error goes to the common editor error handling.

The inline editor panel starts at the row's depth offset, plus for an existing row 23 px and, unless `icons` is false, another 21 px, and 17 px less when there are editor errors. So it lines up with the summary text.

In the main cell's editor, with no Jira dropdown open: Tab, and Enter or Ctrl+Enter while the input is empty, are handled first. While creating an item, Enter and Tab move focus through the creation parameters, Ctrl+Enter toggles the creation clone mode, and if that step handles the key it goes no further. When not creating, Enter and Ctrl+Enter on an empty input are swallowed, so no empty summary is saved, and Tab goes to the common editor key handling, as do all other keys.

The summary sent on save is trimmed. For the Confluence pages promo entry of new-item creation it is the empty string. For a new issue or planning task, the initial summary counts as empty. Finishing the edit of a new row needs a non-blank summary in this input.
While a summary edit is pending, the main cell shows the edited text in place of the server value. The revert link appears only on existing rows with edited data, never on a new row.

'Switch to dialog' is enabled in the main editor only for a new row, when the chosen new-item kind is issue or planning task, outside gadgets and when Jira's create-issue dialog is available. The pages promo content shows only for the pages promo kind. The editor stays open when the creation context changes.
Column key `query-match` is saved as `{key: query-match, params: {queryType, query, aggregate?, distinct?, forestSpec?}}`. Any column of that key is created, even with an empty query.

Without a sum the column requests `{id: query-match, format: html, params: {query, queryType}}`, and the cell shows the value as it comes. With a sum it requests the same in format `number` and the sum attribute `{id: sum, format: number, params: {attribute: <the number spec>}}`, with the total-and-own rules of `summable-cell`. An unset `query` or `queryType` is sent as an empty string. An undefined value shows an empty cell.

The column stores `params.forestSpec` through the 'After filtering' box, but its attributes are requested on the panel's displayed forest whatever the box says, so unticking it has no effect on the total (as the original does).
A `query-match` column sorts by its sum attribute when it has one, otherwise by the attribute in format `number`, with the generic attribute sorter. The first sort is descending.

The default name of a `query-match` column is the trimmed query when it is 1 to 40 characters; otherwise, by query type: 'Text query', 'JQL query', 'S-JQL query'; with no type, 'Query match'. With a sum it is prefixed by the sum sign and a space. Example: query `status = Open`, sum on: `Σ status = Open`.

The attribute picker labels a `query-match` attribute used in a column '<label> (<type name>)', with type name 'Text query', 'JQL query' or 'S-JQL query' (Text when unset). When the label equals the type name, it is replaced by the query with runs of white space collapsed and cut to 40 characters (37 plus `...`), or by 'Empty' for a blank query. The same query and type options serve the attribute editor.

The add-column menu has one entry, 'Query match...', in the Advanced group, which adds `{key: query-match, params: {}}` and opens the configurator at once. The type name is Query match. The column suggests its sum attribute, else the `html` attribute, to the attribute picker. Default width 120, auto-size is not allowed, and it does not shrink when there is no space.

The configurator has, in order: 'Query type', a single-select with Text (`text`), JQL (`jql`), S-JQL (`sjql`); 'Query', a multi-line monospaced input with the placeholder 'Type query here...', spell check and autocomplete off; and 'Options', the aggregate option, always applicable. With no type saved, Text is taken as the value when the list has loaded. The form cannot be confirmed until a type is set. An empty query does not block it.

Beside the query input there is a help link, opening in a new tab: for S-JQL, a link to the plugin's own S-JQL documentation, tooltip 'S-JQL documentation'; for JQL, a link to Jira's advanced searching documentation, tooltip 'JQL documentation'; for Text it is hidden.

Whenever the query or the type changes, with both non-blank, the UI sends `GET /rest/structure/2.0/query/validate` with query parameters `type` and `q` (the untrimmed text), expecting JSON, with a 30 second timeout. The check also runs when the configurator opens. There is no debounce here. A blank query or type sends nothing.

The status beside the query shows: nothing for a blank query; a spinner titled 'Validating the query...' from each change until an answer arrives; a success icon with the tooltip 'The query is correct' when `errors` is empty; an error icon whose tooltip is all `errors` joined by line breaks. A non-blank query with a blank type keeps the spinner, since no request is made.

On a failed request the error icon shows, with a tooltip of the HTTP error text, else the request status text, and 'Unknown query error' as the intended fallback. An answer is dropped when the query or type has changed since it was sent. A validation problem never blocks confirming the configuration.

The Format option offers, in order: General, Number, Percentage, Date/Time, Duration, Wiki Markup. It is stored in `params.displayFormat`, with `params.numberFormat` as the older name. Saved shapes: General removes the param; Number and Percentage `{type, rounding}`; Date/Time `{type: datetime, style}`; Duration `{type: duration, workTime}`; Wiki Markup `{type: wiki}`. The hosting column may rename both params.
A column saved with only `numberFormat` loads from it. The first change in the option writes `displayFormat` and deletes `numberFormat`. When both exist, `displayFormat` wins.
For Number and Percentage a field 'Rounding' shows a choice of 0 to 9, followed by the words 'decimal places'. Default 0. The stored `rounding` is an integer limited to 0 to 9.

For Date/Time a field 'Style' lists the date styles from `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/dateFormatStyle`, sent once per page load and shared by all columns, with a 30 second timeout. Each entry with both `style` and `sample` shows the sample and stores the style; the default is `date-short`. A failed request gives an empty list, for the rest of the page's life.

For Duration a checkbox 'Work time' is shown, with the description: When checked, the value will be interpreted according to Jira's "work hours per day" settings. It is stored in `workTime`, default false.

Only the fields of the chosen format are visible: Rounding for Number and Percentage, Style for Date/Time, Work time for Duration, none for General and Wiki Markup. A hosting column can set each entry to hidden, selected or disabled, and without a setting it is shown and enabled. The option is always valid.

The Period option, in `params.period`, is a single-select with: Custom Period (`date_range`), Today (`today`), This Week (`this_week`), This Month (`this_month`), This Year (`this_year`), Yesterday (`yesterday`), Last Week (`last_week`), Last Month (`last_month`), Last Year (`last_year`). The configuration is invalid with no value.
When the column has `params.timeZone`, the line 'Day start is calculated according to time zone <zone>' shows under the Period list.

Date range options are two date pickers, From in `params.dateFrom` and To in `params.dateTo`. Dates are stored as `YYYY-MM-DD`, and the pickers use Jira's date formats for input and display. When the hosting column says the range is not in use, the stored value goes back to its default, and the option is hidden. The pickers are destroyed when the configurator closes.

With both dates set and To earlier than From, both pickers are marked as wrong and 'Invalid Range. Finish date is earlier than start date.' shows at To. Equal dates are fine. The mark clears when the range is right again, and is rechecked on every date change. It does not make the configuration invalid.

The picker form of the Users option (`params.users`, a list of user keys) offers a multi-user picker with placeholder 'Enter username or email', up to 10 suggestions. With saved users it first sends `GET /rest/structure/2.0/author-picker/users?keys=<comma-separated keys>`, the keys not URL-encoded, and shows a progress state; the answer fills the picker. With none it opens at once. If that request fails, the picker is not created. Each change stores the new list.

The hosting column uses the plain form of the Users option in a remote gadget or when the user lacks user-picker permission; it is a text input holding the saved keys joined by commas. 250 ms after the last key release it stores the text split at commas, trimmed, with empty entries dropped.
